title: Edgar Markov — Vampire Aristocrats
subtitle: Bracket 3 · 3/3 Game Changers · no infinite combos · 100 cards · vampire upgrade pass 2026-08-06

in.name: Vein Ripper
in.text: 6/5 flier, Ward—Sacrifice a creature. ANY creature dies → target opponent loses 2, you gain 2.

out.name: Exquisite Blood
out.text: Whenever an opponent loses life, you gain that much life.

swaps.why: Half of the infinite — pairs with BOTH Sanguine Bond and Vito. Cutting this direction kills all four pairings at once. Ripper is a Vampire (lords, eminence, Roaming Throne) and its board-wide drain DETERS opponents from wiping.
swaps.back: Only if the table explicitly allows infinite combos.

in.name: Cathars' Crusade
in.text: Creature enters → +1/+1 counter on your whole board.

out.name: Bloodthirsty Conqueror
out.text: 5/5 flying deathtouch. Opponent loses life → you gain that much.

swaps.why: Other half of the infinite. GENUINE LOSS — 4/6 field, and its lifegain was a real life floor (replaced by lifelink bodies instead). Crusade gives TWO triggers per Vampire cast (eminence token + the spell), THREE with Elspeth.
swaps.back: Only if the table explicitly allows infinite combos.

in.name: Emeritus of Woe
in.text: 5/4 Vampire. Enters PREPARED → cast a copy of DEMONIC TUTOR. Re-prepares whenever 2+ creatures died that turn.

out.name: Diabolic Tutor
out.text: Search your library for a card, put it into your hand.

swaps.why: Four mana to find a card and affect nothing — weakest card in the 100, 0/6 field. Emeritus is a REPEATABLE tutor on a Vampire body, and it is NOT on the Game Changer list (plain Demonic Tutor is), so it costs no bracket slot.

in.name: Herald's Horn
in.text: Vampires cost {1} less, plus top-of-library Vampire draw.

out.name: Grim Tutor
out.text: Search library → hand. You LOSE 3 LIFE.

swaps.why: Redundant second tutor, and 3 life is real in a deck with no life floor. Horn shifts the entire curve down a pip instead of fixing one card.

in.name: Markov Baron
in.text: Lord + lifelink, with CONVOKE — often one real mana on a wide board.

out.name: Champion of Dusk
out.text: 4/4. ETB draw X and LOSE X life, X = your Vampire count.

swaps.why: At 15 life, X=10 kills you — this lost a real game. Field runs it 4/6, but mostly decks holding an infinite where drawing to 5 is safe because the game ends first.
swaps.back: If lifelink gets high enough that drawing 8 is safe.

in.name: Master of Dark Rites
in.text: 1/1 Vampire. {T}, sac another creature: add {B}{B}{B}. Sac outlet AND ritual.

out.name: Pitiless Plunderer
out.text: 1/4 Human Pirate. Your creature dies → create a Treasure.

swaps.why: Non-Vampire 4-drop. Master of Dark Rites, Phyrexian Tower, Three Tree City and Ashnod's Altar all cover 'dead creature → mana'. Trades a 4-drop for a 1-drop.
swaps.back: If the deck ever wants a 6th mana outlet.

in.name: Urza's Incubator
in.text: Vampire spells cost {2} LESS. Stacks with Herald's Horn = {3} off every Vampire.

out.name: Mind Stone
out.text: {T}: Add {C}. {1},{T}, sac: draw a card.

swaps.why: Vanilla rock with 0/8 field adoption — literally nobody runs it. Cost reduction beats a colourless rock once the curve comes down.

in.name: Phyrexian Reclamation
in.text: {1}{B}, pay 2 life: creature from graveyard → HAND. Recasting RE-TRIGGERS eminence.

out.name: Fellwar Stone
out.text: Adds a colour an OPPONENT's land could produce.

swaps.why: Unreliable — hands you blue/green you can't spend against the wrong pod (2/8 field). Reclamation is the recursion the deck had none of.

in.name: Blade of the Bloodchief
in.text: Any creature dies → +1/+1 counter on equipped; TWO if it's a Vampire.

out.name: Idol of Oblivion
out.text: {T}: draw, only if you made a token. {8}: make a 10/10.

swaps.why: Colourless and non-Vampire. Draw now comes attached to bodies instead. Blade snowballs off deaths, which happen constantly here.
swaps.back: If draw drops badly and nothing better is free.

in.name: Warleader's Call
in.text: Creatures +1/+1 AND creature enters → 1 damage to each opponent.

out.name: Fracture
out.text: Destroy target artifact, enchantment or planeswalker.

swaps.why: CANNOT hit creatures. Generous Gift and Chaos Warp already cover that role and removal stays at the field median of 5.
swaps.back: BLOOD MOON or BACK TO BASICS in the pod — Fracture answers both. Also any heavy artifact/enchantment deck.

in.name: Vampire of the Dire Moon
in.text: 1/1 deathtouch lifelink. Turn-1 play that scales with every lord.

out.name: Oathsworn Vampire
out.text: 2/2. ENTERS TAPPED. Cast from graveyard only if you gained life this turn.

swaps.why: Does nothing the turn it lands and the recursion is conditional. Phyrexian Reclamation does that job unconditionally.

in.name: Teferi's Protection
in.text: GAME CHANGER. Phase out all your permanents + protection from everything until your next turn.

out.name: Toxic Deluge
out.text: PAY X LIFE. All creatures get -X/-X.

swaps.why: The one wipe that attacks the resource you're shortest on. Olivia's Wrath is one-sided and Meathook keeps draining after — two wipes is right for go-wide. Teferi's answers the wipes that kept killing your board.
swaps.back: Vs go-wide opponents when you need a 3rd wipe and can afford the life.

in.name: Smothering Tithe
in.text: GAME CHANGER. Opponent draws → they pay {2} or you get a Treasure.

swaps.why: 2/8 field. Rocks cut 9 → 4 as the curve came down — rock count tracks curve height (the swarm decks run 1-3).
swaps.back: If the curve ever goes back up.

in.name: Charismatic Conqueror
in.text: 2/2 vigilance. Opponent's artifact/creature enters untapped → they tap it or you get a 1/1 lifelink Vampire.

swaps.why: 1/8 field — lowest adoption of anything in the deck. Conqueror is 5/6, the highest-adoption card the deck was missing.

in.name: Plumb the Forbidden
in.text: Sac any number of creatures, copy per creature, draw 1 each.

out.name: Clever Concealment
out.text: Convoke. Any number of your nonland permanents phase out.

swaps.why: Protection 3 → 2, still above the 1.5 field median. Teferi's does it better and Akroma's Will is dual-mode. Plumb is anti-wipe too — sac the board in response and draw 6-8, and unlike Teferi's it beats EXILE wipes.

in.name: Scheming Silvertongue
in.text: 1/3 flying lifelink Vampire. Gained 2+ life this turn → cast a copy of SIGN IN BLOOD. Repeatable draw-2.

out.name: Terminate
out.text: Destroy target creature, no regeneration.

swaps.why: Creature-only removal; Swords and Path cover it. Removal 6 → 5 = exactly median. Silvertongue hits cheap-creature count, lifelink AND draw on one $1 card.

in.name: Florian, Voldaren Scion
in.text: 3/3 first strike. Postcombat: look at top X where X = life ALL opponents lost this turn; play one that turn.

out.name: Impact Tremors
out.text: Creature enters → 1 damage to each opponent.

swaps.why: Weakest of the 3 ETB-damage pieces — Warleader's Call adds an anthem, Purphoros deals 2 and is indestructible. Cost: table damage per Vampire cast drops 36 → 27. Florian is a real draw engine (X is routinely 8+).
swaps.back: If the deck leans harder into tokens.

in.name: Patchwork Banner
in.text: Vampires +1/+1 and taps for ANY colour, painlessly.

out.name: Talisman of Indulgence
out.text: {T}: {C}, or {B}/{R} for 1 damage.

swaps.why: Pain source in a deck with 9 of them. White sources 20→21, pain 9→8, better fixing. Costs one turn of speed.
swaps.back: If you need faster turn-2 ramp.

in.name: Marauding Blight-Priest
in.text: 3/2 Vampire. Whenever you gain life, EACH opponent loses 1.

out.name: Drana, Liberator of Malakir
out.text: 2/3 flying first strike. Combat damage to a player → +1/+1 on each attacker.

swaps.why: Survived a 66-card matrix as the single soft slot — the only card in MV1-3 whose payoff needs to CONNECT. Blight-Priest counts SOURCES not life points (CR 702.15e): 6 lifelink attackers = 6 triggers; a wipe with Blood Artist + Cruel Celebrant = 6 triggers = 18 to the table.
swaps.back: HELD — a fine evasive first-strike body if an MV2-4 slot opens.

in.name: Deadly Dispute
in.text: Sac an artifact or creature: draw 2 and make a Treasure.

out.name: Skullclamp
out.text: Equipped creature +1/-1. When it dies, draw 2.

swaps.why: ANTHEM-DEAD. A clamped token is 3/1 with any anthem out — it lives and draws nothing (CR 611.3c: the token is NEVER on the battlefield unmodified). Deck runs 7 anthems, and Warleader's Call pumps ALL creatures. Dispute is anthem-independent.
swaps.back: If the anthem count ever drops to 1 or fewer.

in.name: Ruthless Lawbringer
in.text: 3/2 Vampire. ETB: sac a creature → DESTROY TARGET NONLAND PERMANENT.

out.name: Welcoming Vampire
out.text: 2/3 flier. Creatures with POWER 2 OR LESS enter → draw. Once per turn.

swaps.why: Welcoming works with 0-1 anthems (token is 2/2) but is DEAD at two (3/3) — and Vampire Socialite's counter is a replacement effect that counts toward it. Lawbringer is a catch-all answer on a Vampire, and the sacrifice is upside (feeds Blood Artist, Celebrant, Blight-Priest).
swaps.back: If anthem count drops, or draw becomes critical.

in.name: Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth
in.text: Every land is a Swamp. Black sources 28 → 42.

out.name: Secluded Courtyard
out.text: Any colour — CREATURE SPELLS ONLY.

swaps.why: Deck now has 28 noncreature cards, so Courtyard was colourless for nearly half the list. Urborg fixes the real problem (56 black pips vs 28 sources), turns every colourless utility land into a black source, AND switches on all four remaining basic-type conditional lands.

in.name: Cavern of Souls
in.text: Any colour for Vampires, and they CAN'T BE COUNTERED.

out.name: Unclaimed Territory
out.text: Any colour — CREATURE SPELLS ONLY.

swaps.why: Same creature-only problem, and Cavern does it strictly better.

in.name: Savai Triome
in.text: W/B/R, typed Plains Mountain Swamp. Enters tapped, cycles {3}.

out.name: Exotic Orchard
out.text: Any colour an OPPONENT's land could produce.

swaps.why: Depends entirely on the pod. Savai is reliable and its land types turn on your conditional lands AND count for Cabal Coffers.

in.name: Phyrexian Tower
in.text: {T}, sac a creature: add {B}{B}. Free sac outlet on a land.

out.name: Battlefield Forge
out.text: {C}, or {R}/{W} for 1 damage.

swaps.why: Fourth W/R land for a colour with only 8 single pips — AND a painland. Pain sources 9 → 8.

in.name: Ancient Tomb
in.text: GAME CHANGER. {T}: add {C}{C}, deals 2 damage to you.

out.name: Mountain
out.text: {T}: Add {R}.

swaps.why: Only 8 red pips in the whole deck, all single — three dedicated Mountains was over-supply. NOTE: Ancient Tomb costs 2 life per tap, the same objection that ruled out Necropotence and Bolas's Citadel; affordable here because lifelink is now 11, but watch it.

in.name: Vault of the Archangel
in.text: {2}{W}{B},{T}: your whole team gains DEATHTOUCH AND LIFELINK.

out.name: Mountain
out.text: {T}: Add {R}.

swaps.why: Rebuilds the life floor from a LAND, costing no spell slot — the direct answer to losing lifegain races. (One Mountain was later restored off a Swamp to hold red at 16 sources.)

in.name: Vault of Champions
in.text: W/B bond land — untapped with 2+ opponents, i.e. always in Commander.

out.name: Plains
out.text: {T}: Add {W}.

swaps.why: White at 21 sources for 20 pips is comfortable. Bond lands are strictly better than basics in a multiplayer game.

in.name: Luxury Suite
in.text: B/R bond land — untapped with 2+ opponents.

out.name: Plains
out.text: {T}: Add {W}.

swaps.why: Helps black (the starved colour, 56 pips) AND the red splash at once.

in.name: Three Tree City
in.text: {2},{T}: mana equal to your Vampire count, in any one colour.

out.name: Plains
out.text: {T}: Add {W}.

swaps.why: Scales with the board — on a wide turn it is the biggest mana source in the deck. Becomes a black source once Urborg is down.

in.name: Cabal Coffers
in.text: {2},{T}: add {B} per Swamp — with Urborg that's ~36 black.

out.name: Swamp
out.text: {T}: Add {B}.

swaps.why: Coffers counts Swamp-TYPED lands (8 → 7 after this), and Urborg makes all 36 Swamps anyway. Funding it from a Swamp instead of the last Mountain kept red on target at 16.

in.name: Sundown Pass
in.text: R/W. Enters tapped unless you control TWO OR MORE other lands — untapped from land drop 3 on.

out.name: Clifftop Retreat
out.text: R/W. Enters tapped unless you control a Mountain or a Plains.

swaps.why: Clifftop needed a Mountain or Plains and had only 7 enablers — untapped just 50% of the time on your 4th land. Critically it was the ONE conditional land Urborg cannot fix (Urborg grants Swamp, not Mountain/Plains). Sundown Pass is 100% untapped from land drop 3. Same colours, pure reliability gain.

in.name: Shattered Sanctum
in.text: W/B. Enters tapped unless you control TWO OR MORE other lands — untapped from land drop 3 on.

out.name: Tainted Field
out.text: {C}, or {W}/{B} only if you control a Swamp.

swaps.why: Tainted Field could sit stuck on colourless for a long time on a slow land draw — only 7 Swamp-typed enablers, ~50% at four lands. Sanctum is guaranteed W/B from land drop 3. Tainted Field is not itself Swamp-typed, so removing it has ZERO knock-on effect on the other conditional lands.
swaps.back: If you want a land that always taps for at least {C} on turns 1-2.

in.name: Anowon, the Ruin Sage
in.text: 4/3 Vampire. Your upkeep: each player sacrifices a non-Vampire creature of their choice.

out.name: Cathars’ Crusade
out.text: Creature enters → +1/+1 counter on your whole board.

swaps.why: The deck had NO recurring interaction — every answer a one-shot except Dictate. Anowon is a one-sided edict every upkeep (our board is Vampires; Roaming Throne is the chosen type, Yahenni is an Aetherborn Vampire). Roaming Throne doubles it; Dictate compounds it. It also turns on seven cards that key on opponents’ creatures dying. Crusade was not a Vampire, missed both cost reducers, and was one of only two {W}{W} cards.
swaps.back: If the anthem count ever drops to ≤1 and you want a counter engine back.

in.name: Tainted Remedy
in.text: If an opponent would gain life, that player loses that much life instead.

out.name: Sorin, Imperious Bloodlord
out.text: +1 deathtouch/lifelink · +1 sac a Vampire for 3 · −3 put a Vampire from hand onto the battlefield.

swaps.why: Sorin’s −3 was seated to cheat an 8-card 5-drop tier into play; that tier is gone (two legal targets remain above MV4), and −3 puts the Vampire in WITHOUT casting it — no eminence token. Tainted Remedy is a permanent answer to the pod’s lifegain decks, and it flips Swords to Plowshares from ‘they gain life’ to ‘they lose that much’.
swaps.back: Tainted Remedy is a hoser — side it out against pods with no lifegain.

in.name: Sangromancer
in.text: 3/3 flier. Whenever a creature an opponent controls dies, you may gain 3 life. Also on opponent discard.

out.name: Vampire of the Dire Moon
out.text: 1/1 deathtouch lifelink.

swaps.why: Rebuilds the life floor lost when Bloodthirsty Conqueror was cut. Each death is a SEPARATE gain event, so it feeds Marauding Blight-Priest, Vito and Sanguine Bond per death — and Anowon, Dictate, Olivia’s Wrath and Meathook manufacture those deaths. Dire Moon was the only vanilla card in the list, doing this job worse.
swaps.back: If the curve ever needs another 1-drop body, Dire Moon returns.

in.name: Vengeful Bloodwitch
in.text: 1/1. Whenever this or another creature YOU CONTROL dies, target opponent loses 1 life and you gain 1 life.

out.name: Markov Baron
out.text: 2/2. Convoke, lifelink, other Vampires +1/+1, madness {2}{B}.

swaps.why: Ranked all four Vampire lords instead of nominating one: Baron is the weakest. Its lifelink is on ITSELF only, its madness is DEAD (no discard outlet in the deck), and convoke saves 1-2 mana and only with untapped creatures you were not attacking with. Stromkirk grants the whole team first strike; Captivating Vampire’s steal is removal (steal then sacrifice to a free outlet). The add is a 5th aristocrats drain — and since Marauding Blight-Priest counts life-gain EVENTS, it is a 5th Blight-Priest trigger per death, not just 1 more life. Curve MV3 -> MV2.
swaps.back: If the anthem count ever falls below 4, Baron is the cheapest way back.

sideboard.name: Drana, Liberator of Malakir
sideboard.when: Ability-light pods where an evasive first-strike blocker matters more than a drain trigger.

sideboard.name: Drana and Linvala
sideboard.when: Facing equipment / activated-ability decks. Shuts off opponents' activated abilities AND steals them.

sideboard.name: Boros Charm
sideboard.when: Wipe-heavy pods. Note it protects ALL your permanents, not just creatures.

sideboard.name: Coat of Arms
sideboard.when: Only when you're the sole tribal deck at the table. SYMMETRICAL — never vs another tribal deck.

sideboard.name: Killing Wave
sideboard.when: Grindy pods, or to break a board stall.

sideboard.name: Preacher of the Schism
sideboard.when: When you want anthem-independent draw. 2/4 deathtouch; attack a player with more life → draw + a 1/1 Vampire.

sideboard.name: Olivia Voldaren
sideboard.when: The only repeatable interaction available. Costs an 11th MV4 slot — take it if the pod is creature-heavy.

sideboard.name: Village Rites
sideboard.when: If draw proves too thin in playtesting. Sac, draw 2, instant speed.

sideboard.name: Gifted Aetherborn
sideboard.when: If you need another cheap lifelink blocker.

sideboard.name: Fracture
sideboard.when: BLOOD MOON or BACK TO BASICS in the pod — this answers both. Also heavy artifact/enchantment decks.

sideboard.name: Patron of the Vein
sideboard.when: Grindy or creature-heavy pods, and against recursion decks — opponents’ creatures that die are EXILED and every Vampire gets a +1/+1 counter. Pairs directly with Anowon. Held out of the 100 purely on curve (would be a third MV6).

sideboard.name: Indulging Patrician
sideboard.when: You need a clock that does not require attacking, or a real blocker while stabilising. 1/4 flying lifelink; end step, if you gained 3+ life, each opponent loses 3 — 18 with Bloodletter, 36 with Roaming Throne too.

sideboard.name: Elenda’s Hierophant
sideboard.when: Token/ETB-payoff pods. Grows on every life-gain EVENT; dies into X 1/1 lifelink Vampire tokens (X = its power, anthems included), doubled by Elspeth. Needs a sac outlet to cash in.
